chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that
one of the Quraysh said to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'By what thing do you precede the Prophets, when you were sent as the last of them and their seal?'
So he said: 'I was the first one to believe in my Lord, and the first one to respond when God took the covenant of the Prophets and made them testify against themselves:'
— so I was the first Prophet who said: Yes. Thus I preceded them by acknowledging God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ: Am I not your Lord? — the divine question from the primordial covenant, referencing Quran 7:172
key_terms.الْإِقْرَار: Acknowledgement, affirmation — here specifically the affirmation of divine Lordship in the pre-eternal covenant
key_terms.خَاتَمَهُمْ: Their seal — the Prophet Muhammad as the Seal of the Prophets (Khatam al-Nabiyyin, Quran 33:40)
key_terms.مِيثَاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ: The covenant of the Prophets — the primordial gathering referenced in Quran 3:81 and 7:172 where God extracted a pledge from the spirits of all prophets

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad precede all other prophets despite being the last sent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that one of the Quraysh challenged the Prophet about how he could precede all other prophets in rank when he was sent last. The Prophet answered that his precedence was spiritual and eternal — he was the first among all the prophets to affirm divine Lordship in the primordial covenant (mithaq), when God gathered the souls of the prophets before creation and asked 'Am I not your Lord?' This hadith grounds the Prophet's superiority not in chronological mission but in the depth of his primordial faith.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Salih Bin Sahl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘One of the Qureysh said to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, ‘By which thing do you<sup>saww</sup> precede the (other) Prophets<sup>as</sup>, and you<sup>saww</sup> were Sent at the end of them<sup>as</sup>, and as their<sup>as</sup> last?’

So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> was the first one to believe in my<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and the first one to answer when He<sup>azwj</sup> Took the Covenant of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>
[7:172] and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord?
So I<sup>saww</sup> was the first Prophet<sup>saww</sup> to say: ‘Yes’. Thus I<sup>saww</sup> preceded them<sup>as</sup> with the acknowledgement in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Mahbub from Salih ibn Sahl fro abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Certain persons of Quraysh asked, ‘O messenger of Allah, by what means have you surpassed the prophets in excellence while you are the last and final one among them to come (with Divine message)?’
He replied, ‘I was the first among them to express my belief in my Lord and the first one to answer the call when Allah made a covenant with the prophets.
He asked them to bear testimony against their ownselves that they have answered, affirmatively to Allah’s Question, “Am I not your Lord?”

I was the first among the prophets to say, “Yes, O Lord, You are the Lord.” By expressing and affirming my belief in Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, as the first one I surpassed them in excellence.’”
